chunks.text: The Total Expense Ratio (TER) is the total of the costs a scheme is allowed to charge for running and managing it, such as investment management, registrar, custodian and audit fees, expressed as a percentage of its net assets. A scheme's daily NAV is published after these expenses are deducted.

chunks.checked: AMFI page: costs such as investment management, registrar, custodian, audit fees as % of daily net assets are the TER; daily NAV disclosed after deducting expenses.

chunks.text: A load on redemption, commonly called an exit load, is an amount deducted from the applicable NAV when units are redeemed or switched out. Each scheme states whether an exit load applies and for how long.

chunks.checked: HDFC glossary 'Load': on redemption / switch out, the sum of money deducted from the applicable NAV.

chunks.text: A Direct Plan is bought directly from the fund house without a distributor, while a Regular Plan is bought through a distributor. Both plans of a scheme have the same portfolio and fund manager, but the Direct Plan has a lower expense ratio because no distributor commission is paid.
